summary.intent: Build an AI agent product (ask-soony) for the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, detect what the plan hides, and act on it via supplier emails and approvals, with a polished UI, demo and hand-in by Sunday 12:00.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition (art books, failed statues, packing speed) and later Standard (clear cases, game cards) miss Sunday 20:00 despite an 'all ok' plan. Built and deployed a polling/versioned-store/LLM-agent app with Today and Launch views, routines, sign-off loop, README and Maren/Felix role views; pushed branch jonas/today-flow. A demo instance with dry-mail mode was in progress.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks or notifications; the only way to detect changes is polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums, because files are replaced under the same name.
data/ (raw portal data, scans, notes, drops) and .env are gitignored; the data is confidential, so no values go into code, commits or external services.
Teammates use CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md as a team workflow; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
Entire hooks log TurnStart/TurnEnd per session and skip checkpoints when no repo files changed; checkpoints are pushed along with git push.
ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK in .env is empty, so Teams delivery doesn't work; push notifications go to every subscribed device with no per-person targeting.
ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds> (off by default) auto-approves a passed-on escalation as the approver, labelled 'simulated for the demo'; real taps win and declines are never simulated.
Prepared routine steps must expire when their case is decided and be deduplicated across routines; otherwise they fail with 'not an open card'.
The shared mailbox sync wrote back a stale copy of the action log and lost records recorded in the meantime; fixed by appending under the shared lock, with a test (commit dd71984).
Routine option matching used a literal 'make po,rev' string instead of separate terms; fixed and covered by a test (commit 67ad2ae). Routines now run immediately on enable or save.
Sign-off approval pages live at /ok/<token> and bypass dashboard basic auth for valid links (basic_auth.py).

code.finding: New module for the approve/decline loop for passed-on cases and internal messages, with one-time tokens that expire at launch and approvals recorded as via='signoff' or 'signoff-simulated'.
Lets valid /ok links through without a password, like the count page; the login page mark was also switched from yellow to ink.
Routine diagram rendered as n8n-style nodes (When, one 'Only if' node with a numbered checklist and funnel, Then steps with a dashed Add step) on a faint dotted canvas.

workflow: Delegating long builds to background subagents while continuing on other tasks worked well, but their output must be committed and the server restarted before it goes live.
Screenshotting in a browser (e.g. pressing J seven times, clicking a decided row) caught UI regressions such as list scrolling and selection jumps before committing.
Confirm before outward-facing actions: supplier emails are real and irreversible, so a dry-mail demo instance was needed for rehearsals.
A cross-check subagent comparing 200 order confirmations and 59 scans against SAP and goods receipts exposed the data discrepancies that the main read missed.
Asking before pushing and reporting the unpushed commit count each time kept the push under the user's control.

friction: The portal token was initially empty in .env, so the API returned 401 and blocked data work until it was filled in.
Five files dropped between 14:00 and 14:37 without notice, so the initial analysis went stale quickly and the briefing page and doc still showed the 14:00 state.
It was unclear whether portal data and supplier replies are identical across teams, and whether sent emails create new portal files; this was left to ask the Lio engineers.
The routine bug sent no email at 07:38, and Today showed four stale prepared steps that failed with 'not an open card'.
Internal messages and escalations were only recorded, not delivered, while the UI claimed 'DC site lead has it now'.
PackRight received two more identical rev C requests after already answering that rev C isn't possible before year end.
The decided-case click jumped the left list to the top because the first Needs-you case was also marked selected.
The sync race condition lost the 07:58 art book approval record, although the email itself went out.
A portal login password was pasted into chat and is now in Discord history.
For the Maren role the top bar still says 'nothing needs you' because it counts Felix's list.

Build a 'What still saves it' section on Launch (latest arrival per blocker, about 900 copies lost per hour of delay).

Combine the four count questions into one case, and send the Pulse note to Hwaseong and the message to Lucas.

Register sender email addresses in portal Settings, and choose the inbox the agent sends from.
